cases.answer: Yuan et al. did not administer any probiotic. It is a two-sample Mendelian randomization study using GWAS summary statistics (MiBioGen gut microbiota; UK Biobank and FinnGen TB data). No probiotic treatment, dose or incidence reduction in patients is reported. The only 'probiotic' mention is an interpretation that order.Bacillales, which showed a protective association, may be a probiotic with a potential beneficial role in TB treatment. The TB review cites Yuan et al. only as genetic evidence that gut microbiota may play a causal role in TB.

cases.answer: The UK-results section calls the 11 taxa only 'suggestive' associations with TB risk (some increased, some protective), and says that they were no longer significant after Bonferroni correction. The later common-taxa section says that three taxa (genus.Akkermansia, family.Verrucomicrobiacea, order.Verrucomicrobiales) had a significant causal association with TB commonly in both the UK Biobank and FinnGen databases. This is stronger wording than the UK section's, and the Bonferroni caveat is not repeated there.

cases.answer: The four samples came from different location types in Abu Dhabi: S1 an urban residential site, S2 an industrial site, S3 a healthcare facility (hospital area), and S4 a rural sewage treatment plant influent. For qPCR (Resistomap HT-qPCR), false negatives were mainly due to mutated primer target sites. For metagenomic sequencing, ARGs with incomplete or low coverage were not detected because of the parameters set in the bioinformatics pipeline.

cases.answer: Across all five training runs, the most influential ANN features (SHAP and permutation importance) were MMSE score, age, systolic blood pressure, total cholesterol and family history. Diabetes and cardiovascular disease were described as comorbidities among additional factors (with sleep quality and physical activity) that also contributed meaningfully to predictions, i.e. less influential than the top features.
